name: Secondaries and GP-Led Continuation Vehicles
summary: Buying LP interests (LP-led portfolio or strip sales), deciding whether to sell or roll in a GP-led continuation vehicle (single- or multi-asset), participating in a GP-run tender, or backing a CV as a buyer. The GP sits on both sides of a GP-led, which is the whole diligence problem: who set the price, was there a genuine market test, is there a true status quo option, is the fairness opinion independent, and do rollers get the lead buyer's data room. Since June 5, 2024 no federal rule requires a fairness opinion, so every protection is contractual (ILPA May 2023 guidance is the standard). LP-led pricing turns on rolling a stale NAV forward (private marks lag at least four quarters), excluding NAV-loan-funded distributions and pricing unfunded commitments. Strip sales and tenders are not treated separately in the bible; LP-led pricing and GP-led process items are applied to them by analogy.
one_check: Get the bid book: if you cannot see how many buyers were asked, how many bid and at what prices, you are accepting a price the GP set for an asset it is buying from itself.

subtypes.name: LP-led secondary
subtypes.description: An LP sells fund interests priced as % of the latest reported NAV; buyer inherits unfunded commitments and GP marks; GP consent applies.

subtypes.name: GP-led continuation vehicle
subtypes.description: Single-asset (SACV) or multi-asset (MACV) CV; existing LPs sell or roll; lead buyer prices; GP crystallizes carry and commits to the CV.

subtypes.name: Strip sale
subtypes.description: A buyer acquires a pro rata strip of a fund's portfolio or of an LP's interests; LP-led pricing tests plus a market-test check (not separately covered in the bible).

subtypes.name: GP-run tender offer
subtypes.description: GP arranges a buyer to offer liquidity to existing LPs; GP-led process protections apply (not separately covered in the bible).

intake_questions.question: Is this an LP-led sale, a strip sale, a GP-led continuation vehicle (single- or multi-asset), or a GP-run tender?
Are we buying, selling or deciding whether to roll?
intake_questions.why: Determines which side's protections matter (price adequacy vs overpayment).

intake_questions.question: What is the reference NAV date and how many quarters old is it?
intake_questions.why: Marks lag public markets by at least four quarters; drives the roll-forward.

intake_questions.question: Is the price at or near 100% of NAV?
intake_questions.why: A SACV near par when LP interests trade at 87% to 91% needs a reason.

intake_questions.question: Do the underlying funds use subscription lines or NAV facilities, or have they paid NAV-loan-funded distributions?
intake_questions.why: Triggers synthetic DPI and recall review.

intake_questions.question: Has the asset been marketed before and withdrawn?
intake_questions.why: Flags the 'could not be sold' failure mode.

intake_questions.question: Is a fairness opinion being provided, and by whom?
Is there a structured-liquidity (preferred equity) component?
intake_questions.why: Adds leverage ahead of rolling LPs; cross-ref NAV lending.

requests.request: Transaction summary: type (LP-led sale, strip sale, single- or multi-asset continuation vehicle, tender), assets or fund interests involved, headline price, reference NAV date and timetable.
requests.format: Term summary from the GP or seller, with the reference-NAV quarter stated.
requests.why: Defines which side of the transaction we sit on and which items apply.
requests.pass: Complete summary with reference NAV date and price as % of NAV.
requests.fail: Price or reference date not disclosed.
requests.verify: Tie the reference NAV to the GP's quarterly report for that date.

requests.request: Transaction rationale memo presented to the LPAC.
requests.format: Memo as delivered to the LPAC, with date.
requests.why: The GP sits on both sides of a GP-led; the rationale must be shown to the LPAC (ILPA, May 2023).
requests.pass: Memo explains why now, why this asset, and why a CV beats a sale or IPO.
requests.fail: No memo, or memo prepared after pricing was fixed.
requests.verify: Confirm delivery date with an LPAC member.

requests.request: Alternatives considered (third-party sale process, IPO, continued hold) with every third-party bid received.
requests.format: Adviser's process summary with bids and dates.
requests.why: CVs are used to hold assets that could not be sold.
requests.pass: Genuine alternatives tested; any third-party bids disclosed.
requests.fail: No alternatives tested or bids withheld.

requests.request: Price as % of the reference NAV and versus the most recent arm's-length mark for each asset or fund interest.
requests.format: Pricing schedule by asset or fund.
requests.why: A SACV at or near 100% of NAV while the GP's LP interests trade at 87% to 91% needs a reason.
requests.pass: Discount or premium explained by asset-level evidence and comparable trades (H1 2026 LP pricing about 87% of NAV overall; buyout 91%, venture 79%, infrastructure 91%, credit 89%, real estate 68%).
requests.fail: Par or premium pricing on a SACV with no supporting arm's-length evidence.
requests.verify: Compare with recent secondary pricing for the GP's own LP interests.

requests.request: Election materials and timetable, including the default election if an LP does not respond.
requests.format: Election notice, election form and calendar.
requests.why: Short windows and a default of 'roll on new terms' force LPs onto worse economics.
requests.pass: At least 30 days to re-underwrite (ILPA materials); default is sell or status quo, not roll on new terms.
requests.fail: Election period under 20 business days or default is roll on new terms.
requests.verify: Count calendar and business days from data-room opening.

requests.request: Fund LPAs, side letters and transfer and GP-consent provisions for every fund interest being sold.
requests.format: Executed LPAs and side letters; transfer clause extract.
requests.why: Buyer inherits unfunded commitments and needs GP consent to transfer.
requests.pass: Transfer permitted with GP consent obtainable on a stated timetable; side-letter rights transferable or identified as lost.
requests.fail: Consent discretionary with no timetable, or key side-letter rights not transferable.
requests.verify: Confirm consent process with the GP or administrator.

requests.request: Latest quarterly reports and capital-account statements for every fund interest, with unfunded commitments by fund.
requests.why: Buyer inherits unfunded commitments and the GP's marks.
requests.pass: Statements issued by the administrator; unfunded commitments tie to statements.
requests.verify: Request statements directly from each fund's administrator.

requests.request: The GP's full portfolio commentary history on the asset(s) since acquisition.
requests.format: Quarterly letters as sent to LPs.
requests.why: Early focus on refinancing, covenants or capital structure predicts worse outcomes.
requests.pass: Commentary consistent with the CV case; problems disclosed as they arose.
requests.fail: Commentary dominated by refinancing and covenant language.
requests.verify: Obtain the letters from an existing LP.

requests.request: Secondary adviser engagement letter, fee basis and who pays.
requests.why: An adviser paid only on closing, by the GP, is conflicted toward closing at any price.
requests.pass: Fee not solely contingent on closing, or contingency disclosed and mitigated.
requests.fail: Adviser paid only on closing by the GP.
requests.verify: Read the letter; ask the adviser.

requests.request: Seller's pricing support: comparable LP-portfolio trades by strategy and tail-end status of each fund.
requests.format: Adviser's market report and trade comparables.
requests.why: LP portfolios traded at about 87% of NAV in H1 2026; tail-end funds at 25%+ discounts (35%+ in some geographies).
requests.pass: Price consistent with strategy and tail-end discounts.

requests.request: Bid book: every buyer contacted, every buyer that bid, bid prices and terms, and the adviser's buyer list.
requests.format: Adviser-prepared bid book with dates; buyer list.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: without it you accept a price the GP set for an asset it is buying from itself.
requests.pass: Broad buyer list contacted; multiple bids; chosen price at or above the best bid.
requests.fail: Bid book withheld, or one or two buyers contacted.

requests.request: Fairness or valuation opinion, the provider's engagement letter and a list of all other mandates the provider has from the GP.
requests.format: Signed opinion, engagement letter and conflicts disclosure.
requests.why: No federal fairness-opinion requirement since June 5, 2024; it is contractual only.
requests.pass: Opinion provided by a firm with no other GP mandate.
requests.fail: No opinion, or provider holds other GP mandates.
requests.verify: Call the provider and check its other mandates independently.

requests.request: Proposed CV LPA: management-fee base (invested or committed), carry tiers, hurdle reset, term, extensions and GP commitment.
requests.why: Rollers are pushed onto new fees and carry on a fresh clock.
requests.pass: Fee on invested capital; carry tiers and hurdle disclosed; extensions require LP consent.
requests.fail: Fee on committed capital with new carry clock and unilateral extensions.

requests.request: Status quo option described term by term: management fee, carry, carry roll and side-letter carry-over.
requests.format: Side-by-side of old-fund LPA and CV LPA.
requests.why: ILPA requires a TRUE status quo option: no change in fee or carry, full roll of carry, side letters carried over.
requests.pass: True status quo option available on every term.
requests.fail: No status quo option, or 'status quo' changes fees or carry.

requests.request: GP's crystallized carry in the selling fund at the transaction price, and the amount reinvested in the CV.
requests.format: Carry calculation tied to the selling fund's waterfall.
requests.why: Carry crystallized on a price the GP set.
requests.pass: Carry calculation disclosed; majority reinvested.
requests.verify: Recompute from the selling fund's LPA waterfall.

requests.request: Carry recomputed at the transaction price and at prices 15% and 20% lower, showing who bears the gap.
requests.format: Our sensitivity with the GP's inputs.
requests.why: Carry crystallized on an inflated mark that the CV buyer funds.
requests.pass: GP economics not dependent on the top of the price range.
requests.fail: GP's crystallized carry largely disappears at a 15% to 20% lower price.

requests.request: GP commitment to the CV as % of total commitments, split into new cash and rolled carry.
requests.why: Alignment: about 10% of total commitments in North American deals vs about 5% in Europe.
requests.pass: About 10% with new cash (North America market); disclosed split.
requests.fail: Under about 5% with mostly rolled carry, or entirely rolled carry.
requests.verify: Confirm funding with the CV administrator.

requests.request: Information-parity undertaking: rolling LPs receive the same data-room access as the lead buyer.
requests.format: Written undertaking and data-room index comparison.
requests.why: Lead buyer receives diligence LPs never see.
requests.pass: Identical data-room index.
requests.fail: Lead buyer has materials LPs do not.
requests.verify: Compare indexes with the lead buyer's counsel.

requests.request: Conflicts disclosure to the LPAC, LPAC minutes and the LPAC vote, with dates relative to pricing.
requests.why: GPs should bring ALL conflicts to the LPAC even if pre-cleared in the LPA.
requests.pass: LPAC voted to waive conflicts before pricing was fixed, with all conflicts presented.
requests.fail: LPAC asked to approve after pricing fixed, or only some conflicts presented.

requests.request: Purchase and sale agreement for the fund interests, including assumption of unfunded commitments and price-adjustment mechanics from the reference date.
requests.why: Buyer inherits unfunded commitments and the GP's marks.
requests.pass: Unfunded commitments priced in; distributions and calls since reference date adjusted.

requests.request: Schedule of unfunded commitments by fund with who funds them after closing and how they are priced.
requests.why: Unfunded commitments are a liability the buyer inherits.
requests.pass: Unfunded commitments funded by buyer and priced into the bid.

requests.request: Structured-liquidity component terms (preferred equity or similar) if part of the transaction.
requests.why: Structured liquidity solutions are about 9% of volume and add leverage ahead of rolling LPs.
requests.pass: Terms disclosed with priority and return; see NAV-lending items.

requests.request: Full company diligence materials as given to the lead buyer: QoE, legal diligence and debt documents.
requests.why: A SACV is a concentrated single-company position; underwrite it as a direct deal, not on the GP's NAV.
requests.pass: Full package received; QoE supports the CV case EBITDA.
requests.fail: Only the GP's NAV and model provided.
requests.verify: Run the Chapter 5 PE request set.

requests.request: Asset-level model and 100-day plan for the CV.
requests.why: The CV case may depend on multiple expansion.
requests.pass: Plan driven by EBITDA growth; exit multiple at or below entry.

requests.request: Return attribution of the CV case: EBITDA growth versus multiple expansion, and assumed exit multiple versus entry.
requests.why: Buyers increasingly underwrite to static or contracting exit multiples.
requests.pass: Case works at exit multiple equal to or below entry.

requests.request: Prior marketing history of the asset: any prior sale process, who was approached, and why it did not clear.
requests.format: Adviser and GP statements; prior teasers.
requests.why: CV used to hold an asset that could not be sold; asset previously marketed and withdrawn.
requests.pass: No failed process, or failure explained by market conditions with evidence.
requests.fail: Asset marketed and withdrawn without explanation.

requests.request: Asset-level debt documents: credit agreements, covenants, maturities and amendment history.
requests.why: Weak assets in CVs often carry stressed debt.
requests.pass: No covenant pressure within the CV term; maturities funded.

requests.request: Old-fund LPA and all side letters, to compare with the CV LPA and to identify side-letter rights to carry over.
requests.why: Side letters must carry over in a true status quo option.
requests.pass: Every side-letter right carried over or compensated.

requests.request: Process-record file: LPAC vote, alternatives analysis, fairness opinion and election-period evidence.
requests.why: LP challenge after closing (ADIC v. US PE firm, Del. Ch., Dec. 2025).
requests.pass: Complete record exists for every ILPA process step.

requests.request: Fund cash flows (dated calls and distributions) for each fund interest.
requests.why: Needed to distinguish dollar-weighted IRR from TWR and check DPI.
requests.pass: Cash flows tie to capital-account statements.

requests.request: Latest audited financial statements of each fund.
requests.why: Marks and liabilities not visible in quarterly reports.
requests.pass: Unqualified opinions.

requests.request: Valuation policy of each fund.
requests.why: Buyer inherits the GP's marks.
requests.pass: Policy specific; independent valuation of Level 3 assets.
requests.verify: Compare marks to policy for top holdings.

requests.request: Asset-level marks for the top holdings of each fund and exit-to-mark history.
requests.why: Stale NAV in LP-led pricing.
requests.pass: Exits at or above prior marks on average.

requests.request: NAV roll-forward from the reference date for public-market moves and known events, by fund.
requests.format: Our roll-forward using public-factor proxies and seller disclosures.
requests.why: Private marks lag public markets by at least four quarters (IMF GFSR Apr. 2024).
requests.pass: Price assessed against rolled-forward NAV, not stale reference NAV.
requests.fail: Price justified only against stale NAV.
requests.verify: Use public comparables and the GP's subsequent quarterly report.

requests.request: Each fund's dollar-weighted IRR compared with a TWR, and NAV marks compared with public-factor benchmarks.
requests.why: Dollar-weighted IRR and TWR are not comparable; marks can lag factors.
requests.pass: Marks consistent with public-factor moves.

requests.request: Fund-level leverage for each fund: subscription lines and NAV facilities, balances, and any recallable distributions.
requests.why: Hidden leverage ahead of the LP interest.
requests.pass: All facilities disclosed with balances.

requests.request: Synthetic DPI excluding NAV-loan-funded distributions, and the recall clause for such distributions.
requests.why: NAV-loan-funded distributions overstate DPI and can be recalled.
requests.pass: Synthetic DPI produced; recall terms understood and priced.

requests.request: Sector exposure of the portfolio, including software share.
requests.why: Portfolios with limited software exposure priced better in H1 2026.
requests.pass: Software exposure disclosed and priced.

requests.request: Seller's disclosure of known adverse events at underlying companies since the reference NAV date.
requests.why: Sellers are sophisticated and know more than the buyer about the tail.
requests.pass: Certificate given with a rep covering it.
requests.verify: Compare with GP's subsequent quarterly report.

requests.request: Tender offer document and GP disclosure of its own participation and of any buyer financing the tender.
requests.why: GP sits on both sides; price set by the GP or its chosen buyer.
requests.pass: Buyer, price basis and GP interests disclosed.
requests.fail: Buyer identity or GP interest withheld.

requests.request: Direct call with the fairness-opinion provider to confirm scope, independence and all mandates from the GP.
requests.why: Opinion provider with other GP mandates.
requests.pass: Provider confirms no other GP mandate.

requests.request: Call with at least one bidder that declined or was outbid.
requests.why: Thin market tests anchored on the GP's own valuation.
requests.pass: Bidder confirms a real process.
requests.verify: Bidder sourced from the bid book.

requests.request: Independent QoE on the underlying asset(s), engaged by us or with reliance.
requests.why: Underwrite the CV as a direct deal.
requests.pass: QoE EBITDA within 5% of the CV case.

requests.request: Our counsel's LPA comparison memo (old fund vs CV, or fund LPAs for transfer).
requests.why: Status quo option and transfer terms.
requests.pass: No unaddressed deviations.

requests.request: Lead secondary buyer's diligence package index and its underwriting assumptions where shareable.
requests.why: Lead buyer's package is the information-parity benchmark.
requests.pass: Our access matches.

requests.request: Executed CV LPA and side letters conforming to the agreed terms, with side letters carried over for rollers.
requests.why: Late changes to status quo or economics.
requests.pass: Redline shows only agreed changes.

requests.request: GP consent to transfer, executed transfer agreement and administrator confirmation of the register update.
requests.why: Transfer without consent is void.
requests.pass: Consent and register update confirmed.

requests.request: Closing statement reconciling price to reference NAV, with adjustments for calls and distributions since the reference date.
requests.why: Value leakage between reference date and closing.
requests.pass: Adjustments tie to administrator records.

requests.request: Election acknowledgement and funds-flow memo, with payment instructions confirmed by call-back to the administrator.
requests.why: Payment misdirection; election misrecorded.
requests.pass: Election recorded as submitted; instructions verified.

requests.request: Quarterly CV report with asset-level performance against the 100-day plan and CV case.
requests.why: CV holds an asset that underperforms its case.
requests.pass: Delivered on time; variances explained.

requests.request: Quarterly administrator-issued capital-account statements for acquired or rolled interests.
requests.why: Marks and calls on inherited interests.
requests.pass: Statements reconcile.

requests.request: Annual audited financial statements of the CV or each fund.
requests.why: Fresh fee clock on an unaudited vehicle.
requests.pass: Unqualified and on time.

requests.request: Notice of any CV term extension, fee change or further GP-led, with LPAC consent.
requests.why: Fee life extended on a concentrated asset.
requests.pass: Consent obtained before any change.

requests.request: Distribution notices identifying NAV-loan-funded or recallable amounts.
requests.why: Recallable distributions.
requests.pass: Source stated.

requests.request: Unfunded capital-call notices on acquired interests.
requests.why: Inherited unfunded commitments.
requests.pass: Calls within the modelled range.

requests.request: Exit report comparing realized price with the CV transaction price.
requests.why: Feedback on GP-led pricing.
requests.pass: Exit at or above CV price.

kill_tests.test: Bid book (buyers contacted, bids and prices) refused.
No true status quo option (rollers forced onto new fee or carry terms).
No fairness or valuation opinion, or the provider has other mandates from the GP, and the GP will not cure.
Information parity with the lead buyer refused.
Election period under 20 business days with no extension and default election of roll on new terms.
LPAC conflict vote not obtained, or obtained only after pricing was fixed.
GP consent to transfer unobtainable, or seller refuses asset-level marks needed to roll NAV forward.

red_flags.flag: Election period under 20 business days (ILPA materials cite at least 30 days).
Default election is 'roll on new terms'.
No fairness opinion, or an opinion provider with other GP mandates.
red_flags.check: Provider engagement letter and conflicts list.

red_flags.flag: Adviser paid only on closing, by the GP.

red_flags.check: Commitment split new cash vs carry.

red_flags.flag: LPAC asked to approve after pricing is fixed.
red_flags.check: Date of LPAC vote vs pricing.

red_flags.flag: SACV priced at or near 100% of NAV while the GP's LP interests trade at 87% to 91%.
GP commentary on the asset dominated by refinancing and covenant language.
Price justified against a reference NAV more than one quarter old without roll-forward.
NAV-loan-funded distributions in the fund history.
CV case requires exit multiple above entry.

metrics.acceptable: Buyout 91%; venture 79%; infrastructure 91%; credit 89% (from 91%); real estate 68%
Near 100% of NAV needs a reason when the GP's LP interests trade at 87% to 91%
About 10% of total commitments (North America) vs about 5% (Europe); under about 5% with mostly rolled carry is weak
Recompute carry at transaction price and 15% to 20% lower
>= 30 days (ILPA materials); < 20 business days is a red flag
At least four quarters to converge after a shock
4% of suits against top and bottom PE firms come from fund investors
metrics.source: HLS Forum 2026, Opting Out of Court

metrics.metric: Yale secondary sale of PE portfolio

third_party_reports.provider: Adviser engaged by the GP; check fee basis and whether paid only on closing
Provider with no other mandate from the GP
third_party_reports.required_when: Always for GP-led and tender; condition of rolling

third_party_reports.report: Quality of earnings on underlying asset(s)

hard_questions.question: What were the other bids, and who declined?
hard_questions.good_answer: A full bid book with named bidders and prices, and permission to call a decliner.

hard_questions.question: Why now, and why not a sale or IPO?
hard_questions.good_answer: Evidence of a tested sale or IPO alternative and a specific reason the CV maximizes value for existing LPs.

hard_questions.question: What is the status quo option, exactly, term by term?
hard_questions.good_answer: No change in management fee or carry, full roll of carry, side letters carried over.

hard_questions.question: How much new cash is the GP investing, and how much is rolled carry?
hard_questions.good_answer: About 10% of commitments with material new cash.

hard_questions.question: What carry does the GP crystallize at this price, and at 15% to 20% below it?
hard_questions.good_answer: A calculation showing GP economics hold up at lower prices and carry largely reinvested.

hard_questions.question: Who provides the fairness opinion, and what else do they do for you?
hard_questions.good_answer: A provider with no other mandate from the GP.

hard_questions.question: Will I get the lead buyer's full data room?
What exit multiple does the CV case assume against entry?
hard_questions.good_answer: At or below entry; returns from EBITDA growth.

hard_questions.question: How stale is the reference NAV, and what does it look like rolled forward for public-market moves?
hard_questions.good_answer: A roll-forward by fund with known events disclosed.

hard_questions.question: Which distributions in the fund histories were funded by NAV loans, and are they recallable?
hard_questions.good_answer: A synthetic DPI and recall clause extracts.

failure_cases.case: Price set by the GP's own mark with a thin market test (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: Selling LPs get too little, or rolling LPs and the buyer overpay.
failure_cases.check: Obtain the bid book and the adviser's buyer list; call a bidder who declined.

failure_cases.what_happened: Rollers forced onto new fees and carry.
failure_cases.check: Compare old LPA and CV LPA side by side.

failure_cases.case: Carry crystallized on an inflated mark (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: GP is paid on a price it set, funded by the CV buyer.
failure_cases.check: Recompute carry at the transaction price and at 15% to 20% lower.

failure_cases.case: CV used to hold an asset that could not be sold (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: Concentrated bad asset with a fresh fee clock.
failure_cases.check: Full direct-deal diligence on the company and its debt; ask why it did not clear a sale.

failure_cases.what_happened: Lead buyer receives diligence LPs never see.
failure_cases.check: Demand the same data-room access as the lead.

failure_cases.what_happened: Buyer pays for marks that lag public markets by four quarters or more.

failure_cases.check: Synthetic DPI; read the recall clause.

failure_cases.case: Abu Dhabi Investment Council v. US PE firm
failure_cases.year: Filed Dec. 2025 (Del. Ch.); outcome not sourced
failure_cases.what_happened: Rare LP suit over a continuation-fund transaction.
failure_cases.check: Process record: LPAC vote, alternatives, fairness opinion, election period.
